body.statement: Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:rare\text{-}history\text{-}alpha\text{-}only\text{-}obstruction}\), together with Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:mixture\text{-}modulus\text{-}length\text{-}lower\text{-}bound}\), shows that on the primitive adaptive-design class no finite constant \(C_\alpha\) depending only on \(\alpha\) can satisfy \[\mathfrak R_{\alpha,\gamma}^\star\le C_\alpha\Omega_{\mathcal D,\gamma}(\eta_\alpha)\] uniformly. Indeed, that comparison and the lemma would imply \(\mathfrak L_\alpha^\star/\mathfrak R_\alpha^\star\ge\eta_\alpha/C_\alpha>0\), whereas the proposition's admissible sequence has \(p_{\min,n}>0\) in every experiment, \(p_{\min,n}\downarrow0\), and \(\mathfrak L_{\alpha,n}^\star/\mathfrak R_{\alpha,n}^\star\to0\). The honest residual question is the following. Fix \(\underline p\in(0,1/2]\) independently of the block counts, block sizes, drift budget, and experiment, and restrict attention to collections of admissible designs satisfying \(p_{bi}(z\mid h)\ge\underline p\) for every \((b,i)\in\mathcal T\), every \(z\in A_b\), and every compatible history \(h\), with the same \(\underline p\) for the whole collection. Does there exist a finite \(C_{\alpha,\underline p}\), depending only on \(\alpha\) and \(\underline p\), such that, uniformly over \(0\le\gamma\le\Gamma_{\mathrm{vac}}\) and every design in this fixed-floor subclass, \[\mathfrak R_{\alpha,\gamma}^\star\le C_{\alpha,\underline p}\Omega_{\mathcal D,\gamma}(\eta_\alpha)?\] Equivalently, can the fixed-floor condition be used to construct two priors supported almost surely on \(\mathcal Y_{M,\gamma}\) whose assignment-averaged observed-data mixture laws have total variation at most \(\eta_\alpha\) and whose \(\tau_W\)-supports are separated by at least \(C_{\alpha,\underline p}^{-1}\mathfrak R_{\alpha,\gamma}^\star\), with the sequential likelihood-ratio or deficiency bound derived from the fixed-floor condition rather than by assuming the target separation? This residual question is not a premise of any proved headline result.
body.justification: The unrestricted comparison is already refuted. This node isolates the strongest directly motivated residual problem suggested by that witness: whether a propensity floor fixed uniformly across the design class is enough to recover a constant-factor comparison, with the constant allowed to depend on that floor.
body.gap: The counterexample uses \(p_{\min,n}\downarrow0\), so it does not decide the fixed-floor subclass. Even there, arbitrary outcome-adaptive propensity updates can reweight future histories, and no schedule-supported bounded-total-variation fuzzy-prior construction currently supplies the required sequential mixture-law bound.
body.consumer: A positive answer would justify constant-factor minimax calibration only for platform trials that enforce one announced propensity floor uniformly over the compared design family. Until then, the NCC implementation must use the optimized radius only as its proved constructive upper scale.

obligation.what_is_open: For each fixed \(\underline p\in(0,1/2]\), prove or refute the existence of \(C_{\alpha,\underline p}<\infty\) uniformly over the bounded-TV schedules and adaptive designs whose every available-arm propensity is at least the same \(\underline p\).
obligation.obstruction: The shrinking-floor rare-history witness no longer belongs to this subclass, but a fixed pointwise floor alone does not make the assignment tree outcome-oblivious. Fuzzy perturbations must obey the control-total-variation constraint almost surely while their induced outcome histories can still alter every later propensity, so the average score-variance envelope does not itself control the observed-data mixture likelihood ratio.
obligation.attempted: The established overlap-measure argument gives the all-kernel lower bound from any admissible prior pair, and the established rare-history construction refutes the primitive-class comparison. Direct two-point and coordinatewise fuzzy perturbations were also considered, but neither yields a uniform sequential total-variation bound under arbitrary outcome-adaptive propensity updates while retaining almost-sure membership in the bounded-TV schedule class.
obligation.partial_result: For the unrestricted primitive class, the established results give \[\mathfrak L_\alpha^\star\ge\eta_\alpha\Omega_{\mathcal D,\Gamma}(\eta_\alpha)\] and an admissible sequence for which \[\mathfrak R_{\alpha,n}^\star=2M,\qquad \mathfrak L_{\alpha,n}^\star/\mathfrak R_{\alpha,n}^\star\longrightarrow0.\] Hence the original \(\alpha\)-only comparison is false. These generic results remain valid on the fixed-floor subclass, but they do not compare \(\Omega_{\mathcal D,\gamma}(\eta_\alpha)\) with \(\mathfrak R_{\alpha,\gamma}^\star\).
